claim: Under MDR Article 32(1), the manufacturer draws up an SSCP for implantable devices and class III devices, subject to the Article 32 exclusions.
limitations: Apply the Article 32 exclusions and the device-specific regulatory context.

claim: In the ClinicOps 8 September 2026 reachable-frame class III sample, 70 distinct records were legacy registrations, 11 were PR-role system/procedure-pack records, and 17 were MF-role MDR manufacturer registrations; all 17 sampled MF-role MDR registrations had linked SS(C)P metadata and were marked validated.
limitations: Systematic sample within the demonstrably reachable public-API frame; not a population rate or full-register audit.
The sample and API behavior can change over time.

claim: Manufacturers are broadly failing to link SS(C)Ps for MDR class III devices.
limitations: Rejected after class- and actor-role-aware resampling on 8 September 2026.

claim: For EUDAMED legacy-device identification, an EUDAMED DI uses the B- prefix and stands in place of a Basic UDI-DI for the legacy registration model.
limitations: Identifier structure does not by itself establish the complete regulatory or SS(C)P status of a device.

claim: ClinicOps treats a B-prefixed EUDAMED DI as a screening signal that the legacy registration is not the MDR Basic UDI-DI linkage target described for SS(C)P handling; this is a derived operational rule, not an explicit Commission rule stating that legacy records cannot carry an SS(C)P link.
limitations: This is ClinicOps reasoning from identifier structure, Article 32 and the MDCG 2026-4 operating model; it is not quoted as a standalone Commission rule.

claim: On 8 September 2026, ClinicOps operational probes consistently served the public udiDiData route around page 30,000 while probes around page 32,000 consistently failed, indicating a deep-offset reachability wall for that route at that time.
limitations: Operational observation at a point in time; not a guaranteed endpoint contract and not proof that the same boundary applies indefinitely.
A 9 September 2026 GitHub Actions canary served page 32,000 successfully, so the earlier apparent boundary must not be treated as stable; see CO-CLM-0011.

claim: ClinicOps observed the public udiDiData route returning at most 50 records per page even when a larger page size was requested.
limitations: Observed API behavior, not a published service-level guarantee; re-test before relying on it operationally.

claim: MDCG 2026-4 described a planned Production deployment in October 2026 for the revised EUDAMED SS(C)P operating model, following a planned Playground deployment in July 2026.
limitations: MDCG 2026-4 is non-binding and the implementation plan can change; verify current Commission status before using the timing after October 2026.

claim: MDCG 2026-4 describes a revised EUDAMED operating model in which the manufacturer uploads the SS(C)P master version and translations, while the notified body indicates the validated SS(C)P against the relevant Basic UDI-DI(s).
limitations: This is the non-binding MDCG position-paper operating model and is tied to implementation of the new EUDAMED functionality; verify current Production behavior before operational reliance.

claim: For devices placed on the market before mandatory use of the UDI/Devices module, MDCG 2026-4 recommends that manufacturers upload SS(C)Ps in EUDAMED as soon as possible and no later than 27 February 2027, with manufacturers and notified bodies aligning their timelines.
limitations: This is a recommendation in a non-binding MDCG position paper, not a standalone statutory deadline; preserve that distinction in client and public copy.

claim: On 9 September 2026, the ClinicOps GitHub Actions canary served pages 0, 30,000 and 32,000 of the public udiDiData route with HTTP 200 and 50 returned items at each probe, so the 8 September apparent page-32,000 failure boundary did not reproduce.
limitations: Single bounded run from a GitHub Actions network context; it does not establish deeper-page or full-register reachability.
Reachability, latency, returned counts and total-element values can change across runs.

claim: Article 32(2)(a) MDR requires the summary of safety and clinical performance to include the identification of the device, including the Basic UDI-DI.
limitations: Read together with the Article 32(1) scope and exclusions; the Basic UDI-DI requirement describes document content, not EUDAMED linkage mechanics.

claim: Following Commission Decision (EU) 2025/2371 on the functionality of the first EUDAMED electronic systems, the Commission's transition timeline gives 28 November 2026 as the deadline to register in the UDI/Devices module devices already on the market before mandatory use, so legacy devices still on the market must be registered in EUDAMED by that date.
limitations: The Decision itself does not state the calendar date; the date is the Commission-stated consequence of mandatory use and should be cited from the Commission timeline.
Some national authorities frame the same window as ending 27 November 2026; use the Commission figure and never cite both side by side.
Whether a specific device qualifies as a legacy device is a manufacturer determination.

claim: Under Article 22 MDR, a person who places a system or procedure pack on the market under Article 22(1) or (3) is not thereby the manufacturer of the constituent devices, whereas under Article 22(4) a combination outside 22(1) and (3) is treated as a device in its own right and that person assumes the obligations of a manufacturer; Article 32 places the SS(C)P duty on the manufacturer, so on ClinicOps' reading no SS(C)P duty arises for a pack registered under Article 22(1) or (3).
limitations: The Article 22 and Article 32 text is primary; the conclusion that no SS(C)P duty arises for the pack is ClinicOps reasoning, not a stated Commission or MDCG position.
Constituent devices keep their own manufacturers' obligations, including any Article 32 duty.

claim: The EUDAMED system/procedure-pack registration records the highest risk class among the devices that form part of the pack, so a class III value on a PR-role record is inherited from a constituent device rather than being an ordinary classification of the pack itself; separately, MDCG 2019-9 rev.1 describes an SS(C)P document-control model in which an updated revision can exist while notified-body validation timing is in process, so a published revision may legitimately be published between validation cycles.
limitations: Sourced from the Commission EUDAMED Information Centre and non-binding MDCG guidance; do not convert a document-vs-record difference into an irregularity without establishing the exact process state.
Do not describe a system/procedure pack as itself a class III device on the strength of the inherited field.

claim: In the ClinicOps September 2026 public-source scan (extraction 8 September 2026), three convenience samples gave 69 device rows across roughly 42 manufacturers publishing national-language SS(C)Ps; in 22 consecutive rows of the second sample no published SS(C)P and EUDAMED record carried the same reference number and revision, the three EUDAMED-held SS(C)Ps in those rows carried a different reference from the published file, the published Basic UDI-DI matched no EUDAMED Basic UDI-DI in 6 of the 22 rows, 5 of 7 multi-language document sets were identical across languages, the systematic class III sample read 95 listing pages (4,750 UDI-DI records; 213 class III rows collapsing to 98 distinct identifiers) with linked-SS(C)P issue dates from January 2022 to August 2026 on the 17 MDR manufacturer registrations, and 103 of 103 detail lookups cross-checked clean.
limitations: Convenience and reachable-frame samples; none of the figures are population rates and the frames saturate toward smaller firms that publish openly.
Content is never retrievable through the public API; 'match' means matching identifiers, never matching text.
Extraction was performed by language-model agents reading JSON; residual extraction error cannot be excluded.
Aggregates only; names no manufacturer and no device and is not a compliance statement about any company.

claim: On the public EUDAMED device API in September 2026, ClinicOps observed that the riskClass= and legislation= query parameters were ignored (totals unchanged), that the same unfiltered query returned different totalElements values minutes apart, that trade-name search is an unanchored substring match, that no 'has an SS(C)P' filter and no Basic UDI-DI lookup exist, and that the systematic sample reached only the lower roughly 47% of the listing because offset pages beyond roughly 30,000 timed out.
limitations: Point-in-time observed API behaviour, not a published service contract; the deep-offset boundary did not reproduce in a 9 September 2026 canary run (CO-CLM-0011) and must not be stated as stable.
Counts are approximate; do not imply full-register coverage.
